ai.description: This slender snake reaches 70 cm. It is reddish-brown with faint white crossbands and a distinct, pale V-shaped mark on the nape. It possesses enlarged, fang-like anterior teeth.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Lycodon capucinus* is best distinguished by its uniform dark brown to blackish dorsal coloration, which lacks the distinct white cross-bands found on most other Indian wolf snakes.
ai.habitat: The Island Wolf Snake inhabits tropical lowland forests, plantations, and human-altered landscapes, typically remaining below 1,000 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The Island Wolf Snake is primarily nocturnal, actively hunting for small lizards and geckos by navigating through crevices and foliage under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Lycodon capucinus* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–11 eggs. Breeding occurs throughout the year, with peak activity often observed during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Lycodon capucinus* occurs in the Indian subcontinent primarily across the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, ranging from sea level to low-elevation tropical forests.
